title: 'Do not disturb' notification briefly visible in panel when going into and out of fullscreen
line: The Do Not Disturb bell no longer flashes in the panel when a window enters or leaves fullscreen, and panels on other screens still show it.
explanation: Focusing a fullscreen window turns on Do Not Disturb, and any inhibition made the notifications applet active, so every system tray showed its muted bell. On the fullscreen window's own screen the panel is still visible while the window animates in, and when leaving fullscreen the panel's old frame with the bell is shown before the state update arrives, so the bell flashed both ways. libnotificationmanager now also reports the screen of the focused fullscreen window, and when that window is the only reason for Do Not Disturb, the applet stays passive only on panels of that screen; panels on other screens still show the bell, and manual, scheduled, app or mirrored-screen inhibition shows it everywhere as before.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: don't show DND on the fullscreen window's screen

The Do Not Disturb icon flashed in the panel when entering or leaving
fullscreen, as the window didn't cover it yet or anymore. When only a
focused fullscreen window inhibits, panels on its screen now hide it.

BUG: 505169

media.caption: Master, panel of the fullscreen window's screen: entering fullscreen (left column) and leaving it (right column), 30 fps frames; the bell appears in both
Same frames with the fix: no bell while entering or leaving fullscreen
Master: Konsole F11 toggled three times, panel area
With the fix: F11 toggled five times, no bell
Master, two screens (left: screen with Konsole, right: second screen's panel): fullscreen on screen 1, moved to screen 2, moved back, left fullscreen
Same with the fix: the panel on the other screen still shows the bell while the fullscreen window is focused, exactly as on master

review.text: Good root-cause diagnosis and multi-screen UX: hiding fullscreen-only Do Not Disturb on the fullscreen window's own screen while keeping the indicator on other screens is much cleaner than a timer workaround. However, overloading the public Settings::fullscreenFocusedChanged signal for fullscreenFocusedScreenGeometry causes spurious signal emissions on an exported library class, and there are two edge-case gaps in FullscreenTracker and main.qml.
changes: Give Settings::fullscreenFocusedScreenGeometry its own NOTIFY signal (e.g. fullscreenFocusedScreenGeometryChanged) instead of reusing fullscreenFocusedChanged and connecting FullscreenTracker::fullscreenScreenGeometryChanged to Settings::fullscreenFocusedChanged, which causes spurious fullscreenFocusedChanged emissions on enter, leave, and cross-screen moves.

Clear m_fullscreenScreenGeometry in FullscreenTracker::setFullscreenFocused(false) so the documented contract (empty rectangle when no fullscreen window is focused) still holds after revokeInhibitions() calls notificationSettings.fullscreenFocused = false.

Use root.showInhibited instead of Notifications.Globals.inhibited in root.inhibitedOrBroken in applets/notifications/main.qml so a pinned or already-active Notifications applet (e.g. with unread notifications) does not still flash the muted-bell icon on enter/leave fullscreen, and guard Plasmoid.containment for null before reading screenGeometry.

reviews.text: Hiding the DND status only on panels of the focused fullscreen window's screen removes the flash in both directions (Nate's delay idea would only cover entering) while other screens and manual/app/scheduled/mirrored inhibition still show the bell, which is a sensible UX. The tracker already re-checks on every dataChanged so screen moves are handled, the single-binding showInhibited plus set-before/clear-after ordering avoids a one-frame glitch, and Containment.screenGeometry vs the task ScreenGeometry are both logical QScreen geometries. Frame strips for single and dual screen clearly prove it; small nit: reusing fullscreenFocusedChanged as the NOTIFY of the new geometry property is slightly unusual but harmless.
